questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **emerged**.

__
 
• The word **"emarged"** is incorrectly spelled. It is not a valid English word. (त्रुटिपूर्ण शब्द)
 
• **"Emerged"** is the correct spelling, which means to come out or become visible from a hidden or obscured state. (उभरना / प्रकट होना)
 
 
• **Example:** After being underground for years, the artist emerged into the spotlight with a stunning new album.
 
 
 
• The sentence uses the word "emarged" incorrectly. The correct word is "emerged," which fits the context of the sentence, indicating the sun becoming visible after the storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

questions.question:

The way Sonam performs live on stage can be called the ________ one.
questions.solution:

• The sentence is describing Sonam's live performance, and the word used should describe the performance in a straightforward, positive way.

• The use of "more perfect" or "perfectable" would be incorrect as they are comparative and imply a lack of perfection.

Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 3.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word:

Grapple
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Release**.

• The word **"Grapple"** means to struggle or wrestle with something physically or mentally; it often implies a firm grip or a struggle to deal with a challenge or situation. (संघर्ष करना, पकड़ना)

 
 
• **Example:** The boxer grappled with his opponent in the ring.
 
 

 
• **"Release"** refers to letting go or freeing something from restraint, control, or pressure; it represents the opposite of holding or grappling. (छोड़ना, मुक्त करना)

 
 
• **Example:** He released the bird from its cage, allowing it to fly away.
 
 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonym of **'Grapple'** is **'Release'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Release**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The two athletes wrestled fiercely during the match.
 
 

 
• **Grumble** (बड़बड़ाना): To complain or express dissatisfaction, typically in a low voice.

 
 
• **Example:** She grumbled about the long wait at the restaurant.
 
 

 
• **Clasp** (पकड़ना): To hold something tightly or firmly.

 
 
• **Example:** He clasped her hand firmly as they walked through the park.

questions.question:

• **Example:** As a novice to programming, she decided to enroll in a beginner's coding course.
 
 
 
• **"Amateur"** means a person who engages in a pursuit, especially a sport or art, on an unpaid basis or someone who is inexperienced or unskilled in a particular activity. (शौक़ीन / अनुभवहीन)

The pineapple dessert was __so delicious that we couldn’t help eat it__.

options.text: so delicious that we couldn’t helping eat it
so that delicious we couldn’t help eating it

__
 
• The phrase **“couldn’t help”** is always followed by a verb in the **-ing** form (gerund).
 
• The given sentence **“The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn’t help eat it”** is grammatically incorrect as the verb *“eat”* is in its base form instead of the gerund form.
 
• The correct substitution is **“couldn’t help eating it”** to follow the correct grammatical structure.

Correct sentence: *The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn’t help **eating** it*.

• **Examples:**
 
 
• I couldn’t help laughing at the joke.
 
• She couldn’t help crying after hearing the news.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts for everyone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Whenever she is coming .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Whenever she is coming"** is incorrect because it uses the present continuous tense **"is coming"** inappropriately.
 
• In this context, the present simple tense **"comes"** should be used instead of **"is coming"**.
 
• The correct sentence is **"Whenever she comes here, she brings many gifts for everyone."**
 
• The present simple tense is used to describe habitual actions or events that occur regularly, which fits the context of this sentence.

Correct sentence: *Whenever she comes here, she brings many gifts for everyone.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + is/am/are + verb(-ing).
 
• **Example:** She is coming to the party right now.
 
• **Usage:** Used for actions happening at the moment of speaking or temporary situations.
 
 
 
• **Present Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + base verb (with -s for third person singular).
 
• **Example:** She comes here every week.
 
• **Usage:** Used for habitual actions, general truths, or fixed schedules.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Ravi said that / his red jacket is / the cheaper than all other jackets.

options.text: the cheaper than all other jackets.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. the cheaper than all other jackets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part **3**, where the incorrect article **"the"** is used before the comparative adjective "cheaper."
 
• When using comparative adjectives (e.g., cheaper, better, taller), the word "the" is not used unless it is part of a specific structure like "the more, the better."
 
• In this case, "cheaper" is simply being compared to all other jackets, so the correct sentence should remove the article "the."

Correct sentence: *Ravi said that his red jacket is cheaper than all other jackets.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Comparatives:**
 
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare two things or entities.
 
• Examples: "taller than," "smarter than," "cheaper than."
 
• Articles like "the" are not required unless referring to a unique or specific case (e.g., "the tallest building").
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Superlatives refer to the highest degree of comparison and are typically preceded by "the."
 
• Examples: "the tallest," "the smartest," "the cheapest."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He is an intelligent person who always thinks before he ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**acts**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a general truth or habitual action, so the simple present tense "**acts**" is used.
 
• The other options: "**acted**," "**acting**," and "**act**" do not fit the grammatical structure of the sentence.
 
• The use of "**acts**" aligns with the subject "He" and denotes his characteristic behavior.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *He is an intelligent person who always thinks before he acts__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Acted**: Refers to a past action, which does not suit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Acting**: Refers to a continuous action, which is inappropriate here.
 
• **Act**: Refers to an imperative (command), which does not align with the sentence structure.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The author's use of vivid imagery ___________ the reader's senses, making the story come alive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**heightens**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**heightens**" means to increase the intensity or effect of something, which fits appropriately in the context of the sentence.
 
• The vivid imagery used by the author enhances or heightens the reader's senses, making the story come alive.
 
• The other options: "**dulls**," "**actions**," and "**confuses**" do not fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The author's use of vivid imagery heightens__ the reader's senses, making the story come alive.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Dulls:** means to make something less intense or sharp, which is opposite to the context.
 
• **Actions:** is unrelated to the context of vivid imagery affecting the senses.
 
• **Confuses:** means to cause uncertainty or disorder, which does not align with the intended effect of vivid imagery.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 Straight from the horse's mouth

options.text: Hearing something that is untrue or a lie
Hearing something from a reliable and credible source
Hearing something that is difficult to understand
Hearing something coming from a horse's mouth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Hearing something from a reliable and credible source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Straight from the horse's mouth"** means receiving information directly from the original or most reliable source. (विश्वसनीय स्रोत से सीधे जानकारी प्राप्त करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The CEO confirmed the news straight from the horse's mouth during the meeting.
 
 
 
• **"Reliable and credible source"** refers to a trustworthy and authentic origin of information. (विश्वसनीय और प्रमाणित स्रोत)
 
 
• **Example:** The scientist provided data from a reliable and credible source to support her claims.
 
 
 
• Hence, the meaning of the idiom aligns with Option 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Hearing something that is untrue or a lie** (कुछ गलत या झूठ सुनना): This option suggests misinformation or falsehood, which does not fit the idiom's meaning.

 
 
• **Example:** The rumors about the actor's retirement were untrue.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Hearing something that is difficult to understand** (कुछ ऐसा सुनना जो समझना मुश्किल हो): This option refers to complex or unclear information, which is unrelated to the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** The professor's explanation of quantum mechanics was difficult to understand.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Hearing something coming from a horse's mouth** (घोड़े के मुंह से कुछ सुनना): This option takes the idiom literally, which is incorrect as idioms are metaphorical expressions.
 
 
• **Example:** This literal interpretation does not apply to the idiom "Straight from the horse's mouth."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**immerse**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is: "A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time." 
 
• The blank describes the effect a well-crafted novel has on its readers, specifically how it makes them forget time due to engagement with the book's world. We need a verb that signifies deep involvement or absorption. 
 
• Let's analyze the options: 
 
 
• **1) immerse:** This means to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest, or to fully absorb someone in something. "Immerse readers into its world" perfectly captures the idea of readers becoming deeply absorbed and lost in the story. 
 
• **2) isolate:** This means to cause (a person or place) to be or remain alone or apart from others. This is the opposite of the intended meaning, as a good book draws readers in, not pushes them away or keeps them alone. 
 
• **3) install:** This means to place or fix (equipment or machinery) in position ready for use. This term is entirely out of context for literature and readers. 
 
• **4) repel:** This means to drive or force (an attack or attacker) back or away; to be repulsive or distasteful to. This is also the opposite of the desired effect of a well-crafted novel. 
 
 
 
• The phrase "immerse readers into its world" best conveys the captivating power of a good book that makes readers lose track of time.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage (with blank 5 filled): *In the realm of literature, words are the (1) **tools **__of creation, and authors are the (2) __**keepers **__of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) __**vivid **__narratives that can (4) __**pilot **__the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5)* *__immerse__* *readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of "immersion" is key to describing a highly engaging and absorbing reading experience, where the reader feels fully present within the story's setting and events.
